newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins rise on FOMC, IMF hopes.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins rise on FOMC, IMF hopes.

text.p: MinFin bonds rose on Wednesday as most investors believe the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee will not raise interest rates and expect the International Monetary Fund to approve payment of overdue tranches of its loan to Russia, dealers said.
"Most investors believe the FOMC will not change its rate and bought Russian paper heavily today," Natsionalny Rezervny Bank trader Denis Pakhomov said.
The FOMC is expected to announce its decision on interest rates at about 1915 GMT.
Sergei Kovzharov, a dealer from Moscow Business World Bank, said that Moscow banks started active buying in the morning, while London banks joined later.
At some point prices reached record highs, but fell later on profit taking, he said.
Expectations the IMF board will approve new tranches of its $10 billion loan to Russia at its meeting on Friday also pushed the prices up.
"The IMF does not seem to have any reason not to approve the tranches," Kovzharov said.

Pakhomov forecast a further rise in prices in the next few days as a possible hike in U.S. rates had already been priced-in and any possible sales would be balanced by high demand for cheap Russian paper.
